summary: The "Dying ReLU" ProblemIn a standard ReLU network, if a neuron's weights are updated in a way that causes it to only output negative numbers, the ReLU will output exactly $0$. Because the derivative (gradient) of a horizontal line at $0$ is $0$, backpropagation stops flowing through that neuron. The neuron "dies" and stops learning entirely.Leaky ReLU solves this because the negative side has a slight slope (e.g., $0.01$). The gradient is never exactly zero, ensuring the network can still update the weights and recover.
